deploy-bot: PRE-FLIGHT ALERT: preflight canary (apac) p95 +28% vs baseline for 4m. Autorevert candidate -> v3.4.4. Options: full canary rollback, partial route rollback, throttle, ignore. link: https://telemetry.internal/alerts/1765432191

June: this is during our 2h change window. Preflight slices are noisy but customer-facing routes are unaffected so far. Thoughts on partial rollback?

Raj: agree partial rollback. If we rollback whole canary we risk rollforward churn across regions. Target embeddings route only (apac).

Mei: embeddings latency spike lines up with recent kv-cache change in canary build. Partial rollback of route=embeddings seems low-risk.

Sam: +1. Throttling embeddings could cause backpressure into frontend. Partial rollback safer.

June: proposed command (will hold 90s):
```
releases rollback --to v3.4.4 --scope canary --selectors region=apac,route=embeddings --reason "preflight p95 spike"
```
I'll wait for objections.

legal-bot: Reminder: include exact audit_id in the release notes and do not use "customer data exposure" unless confirmed. Tag legal if wording implies root cause.

support-bot: Support queue has 2 APAC tickets reporting slow searches in last 12m. I'll prepare templated blurb once we decide.

Raj: no objections. execute.

June: executing now. runout:
```
$ releases rollback --to v3.4.4 --scope canary --selectors region=apac,route=embeddings --reason "preflight p95 spike"
Rolling back apac embeddings slice to v3.4.4...
- drain new conns -> OK
- update route table -> OK
- smoke verify -> p95 within baseline (45s)
Rollback complete. audit_id=rb-20240410-31415
```

Mei: confirming telemetry shows p95 back to baseline for embeddings in APAC.

Sam: support blurb posted to affected customers and tickets flagged.

legal-bot: captured audit_id into compliance bucket. No privileged wording used in customer note.

June: follow-ups: ENG-5012 bisect kv-cache change, keep prod pinned, do not unpin until hotfix or root-cause fix validated. Closing thread when ENG-5012 has an owner.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppressed by operator override at execution time.
